title: Amplitude control: separate transmission from computation
description: The pilot's arm ordering (real +0.025 > shuffled -0.450 > random -1.000) exactly reproduces the pre-learning representational ordering (median sd 70.1 / 13.7 / 4.88, feature RMS 1510 / 839 / 242). So the result may say 'the real connectome carries more signal to the readout' rather than 'the real connectome computes better'. Both are topology effects but they are different claims and the second is much weaker. No control in P4 distinguishes them.
acceptance_criteria: an arm variant with readout features standardised per arm (zero mean, unit variance over a fixed reference set of states) before the heads; pilot re-run with and without standardisation; explicit verdict on whether the ordering survives, i.e. computational vs transmission effect; result recorded in the spec whichever way it falls

title: Experiment harness: build arms, train seeds, evaluate, analyse
description: Ties every component into one reproducible run and writes results to disk so the confirmatory series can execute on the CUDA host and be analysed anywhere. Arms must share input/output indices, adapter shape, optimiser, seeds and budgets - anything that differs besides edges leaks a second explanation into the comparison.
acceptance_criteria: arms built from one real graph with matched controls, both normalisations applied, and identical trainable parameter counts; identical input/output index sets across arms; per-seed evaluation returns a (n_seeds, n_episodes) score matrix per arm; results round-trip through disk with the manifest hashes, package versions, device and host recorded; compare_arms runs on the saved output; a run is explicitly labelled pilot or confirmatory
close_reason: Harness implemented; 146 tests green. The pilot it enabled found a BLOCKING design flaw and two amendments followed. A3: P4's rho=0.95 understated the weight scale by ~1780x for a spiking substrate - 100% of 15,710 spikes stayed in directly-driven input neurons, nothing propagated, and all three arms returned byte-identical scores; replaced by branching-ratio calibration measured with no external drive, each arm scaled individually. A4: spike-count readout leaves the median output unit at ZERO variance across game states unless exactly at criticality; replaced by mean pre-reset membrane potential, and P4's 5 Hz input calibration removed as ill-posed once branching is fixed. Two hypotheses were measured and refuted along the way (hop distance - outputs are 1-3 hops away, 25 of 44 adjacent; gain - a 1000x increase changed nothing); the real cause is sparsity, ~534 of 15,400 neurons spiking. Verified after both: every readout unit varies with game state and arms give different representations. NOT yet a topology result - no learning has run. The pilot must be re-run under the amended protocol.

title: P5 analysis: IQM, stratified bootstrap, probability of improvement, Holm
description: The pre-registered statistical protocol. P5 rules out bare t-tests on means because RL outcome distributions are heavy-tailed and seed-dominated; the primary statistic is the interquartile mean with a stratified bootstrap over seeds (Agarwal et al. 2021), and multiplicity over the two primary comparisons is controlled with Holm at alpha=0.05. Implementing this before any confirmatory run is what keeps the analysis pre-registered rather than chosen after seeing the numbers.
acceptance_criteria: IQM matches a hand-computed value and is unmoved by extreme outliers that shift the mean; stratified bootstrap resamples seeds AND episodes within seeds, and is deterministic given a seed; 95% CI of the difference recovers a known effect and contains zero when there is none; probability of improvement is 1.0 for a dominating arm, 0.5 for identical arms, ties counted as half; Holm matches a worked example and preserves monotonicity; compare_arms reports the exact decision P5 specifies for real-vs-shuffled and real-vs-random
close_reason: P5 analysis implemented: IQM, stratified bootstrap over seeds AND episodes, probability of improvement with ties as half, Holm step-down, and compare_arms delivering the exact pre-registered decision. 18 tests, 127 total green. CHARACTERISED BEFORE ANY RUN (R8): false positive rate 0.010 at nominal alpha 0.05 - conservative, because P5 requires both Holm-p < alpha AND a 95% CI excluding zero while a one-sided 0.05 test matches a 90% interval, putting the effective level near 0.025. Power at 10 seeds: +5pp 0.195, +10pp 0.715, +15pp 0.975, +20pp 1.000; power vs seeds at +10pp: 5->0.465, 10->0.715, 20->0.935. Decision: keep 10 seeds, publish the power curve, and report any null as 'no effect of at least ~10 pp detected' rather than 'no effect'. Also recorded D2: training against real Hearthstone is unavailable - fireplace/hearthbreaker/sabberstone/hearthstone-sim are all uninstallable, python-hearthstone is metadata only, hslog is a log parser, and automating the retail client is refused on terms-of-service grounds.

title: PPO training loop with GAE and seat alternation
description: Last component before the first learning run. Rollouts store the legality masks alongside the action codes so log-probabilities can be recomputed exactly during the update; if the recomputation does not reproduce the stored log-prob at epoch 0 the ratio is silently wrong and PPO optimises nonsense. Seats must alternate per amendment A2's residual imbalance (control mirror favours player two 60.8%).
acceptance_criteria: GAE matches a hand-computed example; terminal-only reward by default with potential-based shaping optional and off the primary metric; recomputed log-prob equals the stored one at epoch 0 so the initial ratio is exactly 1; an update changes parameters and reduces the surrogate loss; seats alternate across episodes; per-seat returns reported separately
close_reason: PPO with GAE implemented and the pipeline demonstrably LEARNS. 17 tests, 109 total green. On a 500-neuron substrate with mirror decks and alternating opponents, 24k agent decisions took overall return -1.000 -> -0.244 and vs board_control -1.000 -> +0.391; the scripted board_control bot scores exactly 0.000 against itself, so the trained policy now beats the bot it trained against (~70%). Episodes per rollout fell 153 -> 45, i.e. the agent survives 3.4x longer. Critical correctness test passes: replayed log-prob reproduces the stored one so PPO's ratio starts at exactly 1. MAJOR CONFOUND FOUND AND REMOVED: MiniCard defaulted to asymmetric decks ('aggro','control') pinned to seats, so alternating seats also alternated decks - and after A2 raised HP to 30, NO policy wins with the aggro deck (board_control: 0.0% over 200 games from either seat). Half of every rollout was unwinnable and half the gradient was noise. A2 fixed one degeneracy and silently created another. P2 never required different decks, so the primary config is now a mirror matchup with no amendment needed. Open item recorded: an untrained spiking policy scores -1.000 where uniform-random scores -0.580, so initialisation is degenerate, not random.

title: Observation encoder and hierarchical action decoder (P2/P3 interface)
description: The joint between the two halves that already exist: turns a MiniCard observation into current injected at fixed input neurons, and output-neuron spikes into a legality-masked three-level action. Per P3 the input and output index SETS must be identical across arms (edges are shuffled, nodes are not), and encoder/readout capacity must be identical too, or the comparison leaks a second difference.
acceptance_criteria: fixed-width observation vector; hidden opponent hand zeroes its block and sets a visibility flag so an empty hand is distinguishable from a hidden one; codec round-trips every action legal_actions() can emit; masks admit exactly the legal set at each of the three levels; a sampled action is always legal; gradient reaches encoder, adapter and heads; value head present for PPO
close_reason: Encoder, codec and SpikingPolicy implemented. 20 tests, 94 total green. FIRST END-TO-END RUN SUCCEEDED: a 15,400-neuron FlyWire substrate (rho=0.95, calibrated gain 3.587, 1,042 sensory inputs, 44 descending outputs, 542,591 trainable params) played a complete MiniCard game - 34 actions, 8 turns, result -1, ZERO illegal actions, 13 ms per decision. The loss is expected from an untrained policy; the zero is the result that matters, because legality is structural rather than learned. IO wiring follows super-class (afferent in, descending out), computed once on the real graph and reused as indices by every arm per P3. Defect found and fixed: act() built its observation tensor on CPU regardless of module device, crashing the first MPS run; unit tests missed it because they never moved the policy off CPU, and a regression test now covers it. Two silent-substrate traps hit: head WEIGHT gradients vanish while BIAS gradients survive when the substrate does not spike, and the 40-neuron toy fixture needed recurrent weights of 25 before signal reached the readout (4 and 10 left it silent) - third independent confirmation that P4's 5 Hz calibration is load-bearing.

title: P4 topology controls: shuffled, random, and both gain normalizations
description: The causal core of the experiment. If the controls are not matched exactly as P4 specifies, any measured difference between arms is attributable to the mismatch rather than to topology. Degree-preserving double-edge swap must run 100x|E| = 31M attempts at the real scale, so it needs batched/vectorised implementation rather than a Python loop.
acceptance_criteria: double-edge swap preserves per-node in AND out degree exactly, edge count exactly, weight multiset exactly, and the presynaptic neuron of every edge (which is what makes Dale's law hold); produces no self-loops or duplicate edges; demonstrably changes clustering/assortativity rather than being a no-op; random control matches N, |E|, weight multiset and per-neuron sign vector while NOT preserving the degree sequence; spectral normalisation reaches rho=0.95 within tolerance; dynamical calibration reaches 5 +/- 0.5 Hz population rate; a graph_stats report covers every quantity P4 requires to be reported
close_reason: P4 controls implemented and validated at real scale. 22 tests, 74 total green. Key identity: directed double-edge swap permutes only 'post' ('pre' never moves), so out-degree, in-degree, each weight's own source, and Dale's law hold by construction. 31M swaps in 11.6 s vectorised, 2.2% of edges survive. Matching at N=15,400: every tolerance-0 quantity identical across arms (N, |E|, density, degree means, rho=0.95, E/I/mod 10,795/3,312/1,293). Graded ladder achieved: shuffled preserves degree tail bit-for-bit (2,843/2,763) and the giant SCC (14,846 vs 14,841) while reciprocity falls 0.225->0.021 and clustering 0.267->0.075; random destroys the tail (42/65) and halves the SCC (7,703). Dynamical calibration reaches 5.449/5.465/4.975 Hz. CORRECTION recorded as R5: P4's second step was justified as preventing inter-arm saturation differences, but all arms fire 0.000 Hz at unit input after spectral normalisation, so without it NO arm learns; inter-arm matching is actually delivered by the structural step (gains differ 3%).

title: MiniCard v1 engine (P2): rules, legality, hierarchical actions
description: Stage 0 of the curriculum: a deterministic, independently-testable card game matching spec section P2. Must not depend on the connectome, GPU, or FlyWire access. Observability is a toggle on ONE engine (Stage 2 full, Stage 3 opponent hand masked to a count) so the two stages cannot diverge.
acceptance_criteria: 10-card pool (6 minions, 4 spells) exactly as P2 specifies; mana min(turn,10); board cap 5; summoning sickness; fatigue on empty deck; hand cap 7; 3-level legality-masked action space (kind / source / target); terminal +1/-1/0 with draw at the turn limit; identical seed reproduces an identical game; illegal actions rejected rather than silently ignored; scripted greedy-face and board-control opponents
close_reason: MiniCard v1 engine implemented per P2, 21 tests, 52 total green. 10-card pool, mana min(turn,10), board cap 5, summoning sickness, fatigue, hand cap 7 with burn, 3-level legality-masked actions, terminal +1/-1/0, seed-deterministic, illegal actions raise. Two scripted opponents (greedy-face, board-control). SANITY SIMULATION FOUND A DESIGN DEFECT the unit tests could not: at P2's HP=20 racing beat trading 88% and games ended turn 5-7, so the optimum was degenerate and no working memory was needed - which would have left no room for a topology effect and not exercised the CX rationale. Amendment A2 raises START_HP to 30; verified control now dominates, games 10-22 turns / 72-139 decisions. My first diagnosis (blaming the removal of taunt) was wrong and measurement refuted it. Residual: control mirror favours player two 60.8%, so seats must alternate and per-seat rates be reported.

title: P1 probe: run subset selection rule, report actual N and |E|
description: Subset size is an OUTCOME of rule P1, not a parameter. MB+CX plus the 1-hop interface layer may land far above the ~8k assumed by P5. If it does, P5 needs its own amendment BEFORE any confirmatory run, not after. Use the aggregated neuron-to-neuron connectivity table (~2.7M edges whole-brain), not the raw synapse table -- fits in 16 GB.
acceptance_criteria: FAFB v783 tables downloaded and SHA-256 hashed into data/manifest.json; loader refuses to run on hash mismatch; rule P1 applied (majority-neuropil in MB/CX + 1-hop interface, syn_count>=5); reports N, |E|, in/out degree distributions, E/I fraction, spectral radius, SCC size; explicit verdict on whether P5 compute budget survives
close_reason: P1 rule executed and reproduced through tested code. N=15,400 (seed 7,918 + interface 7,482), |E|=310,867, density 0.00131, E/I/mod 10,795/3,312/1,293, largest SCC 14,841 (96.4%), rho(W) raw = 1091.8. data/manifest.json pins SHA-256 for all 4 source files; verify_manifest refuses on mismatch. Two clarifications recorded (C1 exact file among 9 connections* variants; C2 threshold applies to aggregated pair not per-neuropil row - observed row minimum is 1), both pinned by tests. VERDICT: P1 survives and produces a scientifically sound recurrent substrate; P5 budget assumed ~8k so N is 1.9x over - resolved by keeping N and specifying per-edge gather instead of dense (R2), with final verdict deferred to fly-ky7.3. 19 tests pass.

title: P5 probe: measure batched LIF+surrogate BPTT throughput on MPS
description: The ~0.7 GPU-h/run figure in P5 is arithmetic, not measurement. MPS lacks efficient sparse matmul so W_rec goes dense, discarding the connectome sparsity advantage. Measure at the N actually returned by the P1 probe, not at the assumed 8k.
acceptance_criteria: dense LIF forward+backward benchmarked at measured N, batch 64, 30-step window on mps and cpu; reports steps/sec, peak memory, wall-clock estimate per 5e5-step run; thermal throttling observed over a sustained run; verdict on whether pilots are viable on the laptop
notes: SCOPE CHANGED by R2: benchmark the per-edge gather formulation (Delta_ij = B[i].A[:,j] over 310,867 edges, ~2.5M MAC at r=8) as primary, NOT dense W. Dense is the fallback comparison only - at N=15,400 it is 0.95 GB and wastes 763x the compute. Measure at the real N=15,400, not the assumed 8k. Anchor: measured 2.81 TFLOPS fp32 on M1 Pro for a 4096^3 matmul.
close_reason: Throughput measured at real N=15,400 / |E|=310,867, batch 64, 30 steps, rank 8, fwd+bwd on MPS. sparse.mm 952 ms/rollout = 2.07 h per 5e5 steps (FASTEST, now the default); dense 2425 ms = 5.26 h; gather 12279 ms = 26.65 h. R2's advice to propagate via per-edge gather was WRONG and is corrected in R4 - index_add on 20M elements is atomics-bound, and torch.sparse.mm is supported on MPS contrary to expectation. A1 gate 2 PASSED at full scale on MPS: all three couplings bit-identical (agreement 1.000000, maxdiff 0.00e+00, 48,727 spikes). No thermal throttling over 120 s sustained (1.01x). Resident memory 2,056 MB; an earlier 128 MB figure was a broken metric and was fixed. 246,400 trainable adapter params at r=8. P5 verdict: 2.07 h/run means ~83 h for the 40-run series on the laptop - confirmatory belongs on the CUDA host as A1 already required; P5's budget there stays UNVERIFIED pending fly-ky7.4.

title: Bootstrap reproducible Python env on dev host (M1 Pro)
description: Amendment A1 requires a single pinned lockfile shared by the M1 Pro dev host and the CUDA desktop. Homebrew Python 3.14.7 is PEP 668 externally-managed, so a venv is mandatory. torch 2.14.0 has an arm64/cp314 wheel.
acceptance_criteria: venv created; lockfile pins torch, brian2, scipy, pandas, networkx, pyarrow; torch.backends.mps.is_available() returns True; brian2 imports and runs a 2-neuron smoke sim; lockfile resolves on both hosts
close_reason: Env bootstrapped on dev host. uv venv on Python 3.13.15; uv.lock pins torch 2.14.0, brian2 2.10.1, scipy 1.18.1, pandas 3.0.5, networkx 3.6.1, pyarrow 25.0.1, numpy 2.5.3. tests/test_env.py: 9 passed. MPS verified beyond is_available() with a real 512x512 matmul+backward; measured 2.81 TFLOPS fp32 on 4096^3 matmul. Brian2 2-neuron LIF smoke sim spikes as expected. NOT verified: execution on the CUDA host - split out as a separate task rather than claimed.

title: Verify lockfile resolves and runs on the CUDA desktop
description: Amendment A1 requires ONE lockfile working on both hosts. On the M1 Pro the lock is universal (55 manylinux entries, requires-python ==3.13.*) but execution on the CUDA host could not be verified from the dev machine. Must pass before any confirmatory run, since P5's 40-run series lives on that host.
acceptance_criteria: uv sync succeeds on the CUDA desktop from the committed uv.lock; tests/test_env.py passes there; test_an_accelerator_is_available reports cuda=True; torch reports the expected CUDA version

title: Design FlyWire-constrained Hearthstone research program
description: Determine whether a FlyWire-constrained spiking neural substrate can learn sequential decisions in a Hearthstone-like environment; establish evidence-backed architecture, curriculum, data access, compute limits, baselines, ablations, MVP, and publication-grade experiment.
notes: PROTOCOL LOCKED 2026-09-16. All six pre-registration items fixed in .omc/specs/deep-interview-flywire-hearthstone.md (section 'Pre-Registered Protocol', P1-P6). Decisions: MB+CX subset on FAFB v783 (syn_count>=5, majority-neuropil + 1-hop); MiniCard v1 env spec complete (rules, obs mask, 3-level action hierarchy, potential-based shaping, held-out set); masked low-rank adapter (B@A)*M_arm with r=8 primary and {2,8,32} sweep secondary; 10 seeds x 5e5 env steps x 4 arms (~30 GPU-h on 4070 Ti) with all-arms escalation rule; IQM + stratified bootstrap + Holm; PyTorch CUDA for learning, Brian2 CPU for spike-train cross-check. Next: decompose into implementation tasks. No code written yet.
